Issue #534 output bundle. A bounded CLEAN_ROOM canary ran on 2026-08-22 against a disposable single-node core (refcore, sha256 4ea664cc6bae1d3a999bf4293ad65136821c3a611a498894d428448a1610d127) that is deliberately not committed, with provider_activation NOT_PERFORMED and cost 0.00 USD; its receipts are the bundle under data/handoff/git-at-any-scale/. That run does not select or admit a hosting-grade runtime: it has one authority process, zero replicas, one cache, no socket layer, one local filesystem, one monotonic clock and SIGKILL-only fault injection, so power loss, media failure, network partition, clock skew, replica fan-out, elasticity and gossip have no fault surface to exercise. Human authority still owns provider activation, account, spend ceiling, service terms, data location, a pinned benchmark host and teardown, and only an admitted non-clean-room subject gives the durability/linearizability/stale-cache/gossip-loss/compaction/corruption/matched-scale experiments a hosting-grade command contract. The two commands above are the harness controls that survive without such a subject; neither replays the canary, because the recorded runtime digest lives only in the disposable scratchpad.

Independent Shadow finding SR-01 in data/handoff/git-at-any-scale/issue-535-shadow-receipt.json. The bundle's own law is to record absent lanes as NOT_EXERCISED rather than infer them, and it lists five such entries; eight further required items are absent from the bundle with no entry at all. Absent workload classes: concurrent pushes to disjoint refs; clone/fetch/read during writes; idle repository scaled down then reactivated; compaction during normal traffic. Absent metrics: memory; retries (cas_conflicts is recorded, retries is not); disk/network/object-store request counts (bytes are recorded, requests are not); fault recovery time. Each must be executed or given an explicit NOT_EXERCISED entry before this item can claim a complete denominator, and the negative control must be bound to the committed history rather than to a sibling run.
